name: Linux File Permissions
description: Ability to understand and manage permissions and ownership of files and directories in Linux.

evaluation_concepts.name: Permission Classes
evaluation_concepts.description: Understands that Linux permissions are evaluated separately for owner, group, and others.
evidence_criteria: Identifies owner, group, and others as distinct permission classes.
Explains that different permissions may apply to each class.
common_misconceptions: Treats permissions as identical for all users.
Confuses owner permissions with group or others permissions.

evaluation_concepts.name: Read Write Execute
evaluation_concepts.description: Understands the meaning and practical effect of read, write, and execute permissions.
evidence_criteria: Explains read as reading file contents.
Explains write as modifying file contents.
Explains execute as executing a regular file where applicable.
common_misconceptions: Claims write permission means permission to change permission bits.
Claims execute permission permits modifying file contents.
Treats read, write, and execute as interchangeable.

evaluation_concepts.name: Numeric Permissions
evaluation_concepts.description: Understands numeric permission notation such as 755 and 644 and how digits map to permission classes.
evidence_criteria: Maps the three digits to owner, group, and others.
Understands numeric values represent combinations of read, write, and execute.
Correctly interprets common values such as 755 or 644.
common_misconceptions: Treats 755 as the same permission for everyone.

evaluation_concepts.name: chmod
evaluation_concepts.description: Understands that chmod changes file or directory permission bits.
evidence_criteria: Identifies chmod as the command used to change permission bits.
Provides or correctly interprets a valid chmod example.
common_misconceptions: Uses chmod as if it changes process resources.

evaluation_concepts.name: chown
evaluation_concepts.description: Understands that chown changes file or directory ownership and distinguishes ownership from permission bits.
evidence_criteria: Identifies chown as the command used to change ownership.
common_misconceptions: Claims chown changes rwx permission bits.

evaluation_concepts.name: Directory Permissions
evaluation_concepts.description: Understands that read, write, and execute have different practical meanings for directories.
evidence_criteria: Explains that read on a directory relates to listing entries.
Explains that execute on a directory is required to traverse/search it.
Recognizes that directory permission semantics differ from regular files.
common_misconceptions: Claims execute on a directory means running the directory as a program.
Assumes regular-file and directory permission semantics are identical.

evaluation_concepts.name: Security Implications
evaluation_concepts.description: Understands security and operational consequences of inappropriate Linux permissions.
evidence_criteria: Recognizes risk from unnecessarily broad permissions.
Explains why permissions such as 777 may be undesirable.
Reasons about least privilege or minimum required access.
common_misconceptions: Claims broader permissions always improve security.

depth_scale.1: Basic awareness or recognition with minimal explanation.
depth_scale.3: Correct practical application, example, configuration, or troubleshooting.
depth_scale.4: Deep reasoning involving edge cases, trade-offs, limitations, interactions, security implications, or operational consequences.

principles: Do not infer knowledge solely from keyword presence.
A concept name or command name alone is not sufficient for conceptual depth.
Do not award evidence for knowledge not demonstrated in this answer.
Distinguish conceptual understanding from procedural memorization.
Identify explicit technically incorrect claims separately from demonstrated evidence.
Do not treat claimed experience or confidence as evidence.
When evidence is ambiguous, prefer the lower justified depth.
